Commentary.Commentary: The game is in the balance now with both sides wrestling for the advantage.

Philander led the pace charge today and debutant Maharaj was brilliant too as the tourists maintained relentless pressure on the Aussie batsmen. South Africa missed Steyn this session but it didn't matter as the others finished off things remarkably well. The track is still having good pace and carry with slight movement too. However, it's certainly a good pitch but you just cannot bat loosely. The game is level at this point and the next session should be fun. Join us in a while for the final session of the day.

Exceptional comeback by South Africa after being on the mat yesterday. Australia were cruising at 158/0 but once David Warner departed narrowly short of a ton, the rest meekly capitulated against some superb bowling. Shaun Marsh couldn't carry on either and it was a procession from there on as the 10 wickets fell for just 86 runs. Voges and Nevill got a start but failed to carry on while Siddle's cameo got Australia past the Protea total.

OUT! Philander has wrapped it up! Full and outside off, a bit of shape away as Lyon flashes at it but gets a thick edge that flies low to third slip where Elgar snaps it up. What a comeback this is from SA today! Absolutely incredible! Australia have been bowled out for 244, lead by just 2. TEA HAS BEEN TAKEN EARLY ON DAY 2.
Full and outside off, blocked off the front foot towards mid off. Philander has overstepped.
Nathan Lyon is the last man in.

OUT! Soft, soft dismissal! Length ball outside off, Hazlewood plays it with an angled bat and offers catching practice to gully where Duminy takes it with minimum fuss. Cannot blame a tailender for this kind of shot but nevertheless, Hazlewood should have tried something better.
Vernon Philander is back on.
In the air....safe! Australia into the lead. Floated ball on off, Hazlewood steps out to play the lofted stroke but gets a big leading edge that just clears mid off. Single taken.
Flatter on off, punched off the back foot to long on for a single. SCORES LEVEL NOW.
Floated outside off, Siddle pushes at it but gets an inside edge on to the pads.
Full outside off, Siddle reaches out and defends it well.
Slider outside off, Hazlewood stays back and glides it with an angled bat towards third man. Won't make the fence but three more taken.
Flatter outside off, Hazlewood stays back and defends it solidly.
Pitched up on middle, Siddle gets across and digs it out towards mid on.
Good length outside off, defended well off the back foot.
Fuller outside off, Siddle bunts it through the covers for a brace.
FOUR! Good shot! Short on middle, Siddle swivels and pulls it hard to the deep square leg fence for a boundary. Controlled shot and that's a valuable boundary for the Aussies. The deficit is now 6.
Full and on off, worked away to the leg side.
Fuller on middle, Siddle bunts it to mid on.
Flatter outside off, blocked well off the back foot to the off side.
Josh Hazlewood is the number 10 batsman.

OUT! Maharaj has his third! What a debut game he is having after a horror start! Floated outside off, Nevill steps out to push at it but the ball lobs towards gully where Amla takes it very well after moving to his right from slip. Appeal for a catch as SA feel there is an inside edge that's rebounded off the pad. The umpire's finger is raised straightaway. Replays do not confirm anything. No reviews left anyway and so Nevill has to go.
Flatter down the leg side, Nevill looks to flick but misses.
Fuller outside off, defended well off the front foot to the off side.

SIX! Smoked! Floated on middle and leg, Nevill dances down the track and clobbers it comfortably over long on for a maximum. This is turning out to be a vital little knock from Nevill. Deficit is now just 10.
Flatter on off, Nevill hangs back and blocks it strongly on to the pitch.
Fuller outside off, Siddle defends it nicely off the front foot.
Speared well down the leg side, no stroke offered to that one.

Not out! Dug in short on off, Siddle ducks but this doesn't rise as much and raps him on the body. Appeal for lbw that is turned down by the umpire. SA decide to review the decision. Hot Spot and Snicko don't detect any bat or glove. It has hit him on the forearm and then rolled towards point. Ball Tracker shows it going well over the stumps. Llong was also citing height when he turned down the appeal. The on-field call stays and Siddle escapes.
South Africa have taken a review for lbw against Siddle. He isn't offering a stroke.
Fuller on the pads, worked away to the leg side for a single.
Full and outside off, defended well off the front foot.

FOUR! Another boundary! That's the third in the last six balls and Australia are getting some breathing space now. Length ball wide outside off, Nevill feasts on it with a glide through backward point to find the fence.
Floated on middle, Siddle steps to block and gets it off the inside half to the leg side.
Fuller outside off, blocked well off the front foot.
FOUR! Clean strike! Floated on middle and off, Siddle step out to that one and lofts it cleanly over mid on. Good stroke and that races away to the fence for a boundary.
Full outside off, Siddle steps out to block but gets an inside edge on the pads.

FOUR! Risky but pays off! A bit short on middle and off, sliding in as Siddle looks to cut. No room at all and he gets a thickish edge that flies well past slip to the third man fence. Handy runs these for Australia.
Drifting in from outside off, Siddle steps out to that one and blocks it.
Short ball and Nevill ducks instantly under the pacy bumper.
Outside off, Nevill doesn't offer a shot to that one.
Full and outside off, Nevill pushes at it but is beaten.
Fullish on middle and leg, Siddle gets across and whips it away through wide mid on. The ball goes to the deep as the batsmen get three more.
Fullish on leg stump, Siddle shuffles to flick but is struck on the pads. Muted lbw appeal that is turned down.
Full and outside off, Nevill jams it to the covers. Single taken.
Floated outside off, Siddle reaches out and blocks it out.
Quicker ball around leg stump, Siddle is rapped on the pads and this time there is no bat involved. Missing leg clearly though.
Drifting in on middle and leg, Siddle steps out and drives it to mid on.
Flatter outside off, pushed off the back foot towards backward point.
Flatter on middle, Siddle plays back to that one and is lucky to get an inside edge on to the pads. He was close to being lbw there.
Floated outside off, Nevill steps out and drives it down to long off for a single.
Fuller on middle and leg, Nevill glances it down to fine leg for a single.
Length ball outside off, Nevill defends it firmly from the crease.
FOUR! Lucky runs! Full and wide outside off, Nevill goes for a wild drive without any footwork. Gets a thick edge that flies between the slips and gully to the third man fence.
On middle and leg, Nevill works it to the leg side.
Good length around off, extra bounce to rap Nevill on the thigh pad.
Short ball and Nevill ducks under bouncer.
Peter Siddle is in next.

OUT! Faf du Plessis takes a sharp catch and Starc bags a duck! Flighted ball on middle, fuller in length, Starc winds up for a flick shot but fails to middle it. It comes off the inside half of the bat, loops towards short mid-wicket where du Plessis dives to his left and snaps a good low catch. Australia going down quickly.
Slower on off, Starc gets back and pushes it to covers.
Landing on middle, Starc goes back to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tosses it up and lands it outside off, Starc tries to drive but misses.
Dances down the track and pushes it to mid off for a quick single. The throw towards the keeper is quite wide and Starc reaches the other end safely.
Mitchell Starc arrives. He averages 111 at this venue.

OUT! Rabada strikes! Massive setback for the Aussies as the last proper batsman departs. A full length ball angling into the batsman, swinging in, Voges falls over to the off side as he attempts to flick it on the leg side but he closes the face of the bat early and the ball pops out of the leading edge. Rabada takes the return catch with ease and Australia lose their sixth wicket. They still trail by 40 runs!
Bowls it full and on off, Voges defends it with soft hands to the off side.
Back of a length ball on off, Adam stands tall inside the crease and punches it through point for a couple of runs.
Full and angling into the batsman, it straightens a shade after landing, Voges gets squared up a bit and defends it to the off side.
Lands it very full and outside off, Voges chases it and mistimes his drive towards the cover fielder.
Fullish and angling into the batsman, Nevill defends it off his front foot to short cover.
Floated full ball on middle, defended back with a straight bat.
Slower through the air and around off, Nevill goes back and defends it to the off side.
Fires a quicker one on the pads, it's worked away through backward square leg and Abbott (sub) in the deep makes the stop. One run added to the total. 200 up for Australia!
Flighted and full on off, it's defended off the front foot to the off side.
Voges has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! That's a fine shot! Voges advances down to the pitch of the delivery which is around leg and whips it through the gap at mid-wicket and mid on for a boundary. Nice balance and timing on that occasion.
Too full in length and angled into the batsman, Nevill digs it out back to the bowler. It goes on one bounce and Rabada jumps to make a half stop. Deflects it towards short cover.
Good length delivery outside off, Peter allows it through to the keeper.
Full in length and outside off, Nevill plays it from the crease and pushes it to covers.
A steamy bouncer, around off, Nevill crouched a bit and then leans back to let it through to the keeper.
Big swing on this occasion, landing around off and curling down, Voges gets forward and across and  nudges it through backward square leg for a single.
Back of a length ball around off, Voges goes on his toes as he defends it to the off side.
Tossed up ball on off, Nevill gets on the front foot and pushes it firmly. It hits the silly point fielder.
Floated one on off, Nevill defends it close to his front pad.
Loopy and on middle, a straight batted defense offered by Peter.
Quicker and flatter on off, Nevill is on the front foot and defends it to the off side.
Advances down the track to a full ball and pushes it towards mid on.
Floated full ball on middle, defended back with a straight bat.
Bouncer on off, Voges ducks to end the over.
Rabada bowls it full around off and forces the batsman on the front foot, Voges defends it with gentle hands.
Remains inside the crease and defends it on the leg side.
FOUR! It's a poor delivery, short and wide outside off, Voges rocks back and spanks it through backward point for a cracking boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length ball angling into the batsman, Voges defends it off his back foot.
Kagiso Rabada replaces Philander in the attack.
Nevill has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy and drifting into the batsman, Nevill advances down the track, gets deceived a bit in flight but does well to push it towards mid off.
Presses forward to a full ball and drives it back to the bowler.
Lunges to a full one this time and defends it to the off side.
Arm ball on middle, a bit on the shorter side, Peter goes back and defends it to mid-wicket.
Full and on off, skidding in, Nevill defends it by prodding forward.
Fuller and on off, it's defended off the front foot this time. It's been an impressive spell by Vernon.
Good length ball on off, coming back in a shade, Voges goes back in defense.
Pitches it further up to the batsman, around off, Voges gets forward and pushes it firmly back past the bowler to mid off.
Good length delivery in the zone outside off, allowed through to the keeper.
A little short and on off, it's gently tapped towards point for a single.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Presses forward to a full ball again and drives it gently in front of mid off. They cross for a quick single as the fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end.
Strides forward to a full ball and defends it back to the bowler.
Walks down the track and hits it across the line. Once again a diving stop by the mid-wicket fielder, Duminy. No run taken.
Tossed up ball on leg, defended.
Nevill has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy and full ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Length ball on middle, tucked off the pads to mid-wicket.

EDGED AND FOUR! Philander bowls it on a full length and lands it just outside off, shaping away again, Voges with zero footwork has a nervous push inside the line and edges it behind. De Kock dives to his right but it falls just wide of him and sneaks past first slip for a boundary. On the lighter side, it's a great placement, although not an intended one.
Good length ball on off, Voges nicely gets behind the line and offers a straight bat in defense.
Philander bowls it full and wide outside off, a hint of away shape, Voges gets forward to cover the line and then shoulders arms.
Full in length and just outside off, Adam strides forward and defends it to short cover.
Presents the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it softly to silly point.
Full toss around leg, Voges steps down the track and hits it across the line. Duminy moves across to his left from mid-wicket and makes a diving stop. A single taken.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and blocks it safely.
Lunges to a full ball and dead bats it on the off side, in front of silly point to be precise.
Loopy full ball on middle, Voges gets on the front foot and defends it to the leg side.
Flatter and around middle, skidding down, Nevill taps it in front of square leg and pinches a quick single.
Too straight in line on this occasion, Nevill quietly nudges it behind square leg for a single. Off the mark now.
Angles in a length ball on middle, Nevill has to play at it and does so with a straigt bat. He keeps it out safely on the leg side. Philander has stepped up his performance in Steyn's absence.
Pitches it full and outside off, nipping away, another leave by the Aussie wicketkeeper batsman.
Full and outside off, moving away, Nevill has a patient leave.
Angles it on a length around off, Nevill stays back, gets squared up a bit and defends it to the off side.
Peter Nevill strides in next.

OUT! Marsh has been adjudged lbw! Philander strikes again and Australia have now lost half their side. He hurls in a length ball on off, shaping in a bit, Marsh fails to defend it from the crease and it hits him on the back leg. They appeal and the finger goes up. A disappointing outing with the bat for the younger Marsh, bags a duck. Australia still trail by 61 runs!
Jumps out of the crease to a full ball and hits it to short mid-wicket.
A touch short and on off, Adam goes back and punches it straight to covers.
Too full in length on off, Voges forces it through the line, past the bowler but straight to mid off.
Uses his feet to get down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Flighted and on middle, Voges brings his bat in front of the pads in defense.
Loopy and full on off, Voges defends it off his front foot.
Philander hurls across a full swinging delivery outside off, Marsh watches the line closely and leaves it untouched.
Outside off on a length, tapped down to point.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Angles in a length ball on off, Marsh defends it from the crease.
What happened there? Umpire Llong has chat with Faf. Probably about some chatter that has gone overboard by the SA fielders. Not sure though but Faf seemed to agree with the advice he is given.
On a length and outside off, Marsh allows it through.
Good length outside off, Marsh blocks it solidly off the front foot.
Arm ball on middle, drifting down, Voges lunges to defend but misses and is hit on the pads.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot again.
Loopy full ball on off, Adam draws forward in defense.

Flighted and on off, Voges goes hard at it but get an inside edge onto the boot. It pops out and then falls safely in the middle of the pitch. No takers for it as the close-in fielders were taking cover as Voges had gone after it with attacking intent.
Maharaj drags his length short and lands it on off, Voges goes back and cuts it to point, but straight to the fielder.
Tossed up ball on off, Voges lunges and defends it in front of silly point.
Keshav Maharaj to bowl from the other end...
Full length ball angling into the right-hander, Marsh defends it off his pads to short mid-wicket. End of a longish over.
Here we go, everything sorted out it seems.

There seems to be a delay due to sightscreen. It has got stuck and is refusing to move. The groundsmen are trying to fix the issue. It's taking ages and is really frustrating for everyone. The players and umpires are helplessly waiting, so are we!

We're back for the afternoon session. This game is nicely poised now after a heroic comeback by South Africa in the morning. Australia need partnerships to take a substantial first innings lead which is exactly what South Africa would like to avoid. Promises to be an entertaining next couple of hours. The players are back on and Mitchell Marsh is the new batsman, replacing his elder brother. Vernon Philander to complete his over...
...DAY 2, SECOND SESSION...

South Africa badly needed such a session and they will be relieved. All the three pacers bowled with great pace and control, getting the ball to reverse appreciably as well. Steyn's exit midway due to injury seemed like a body blow for the visitors but the man who filled up for him, debutant Maharaj did the trick by getting the big scalp of Smith. The hosts are still only a partnership away from taking the lead but this is a testing phase for them. Join us in a while for the second session.

South Africa are back into the game with a bang. Four wickets and just 76 runs in the morning session as the visitors managed to recover some ground after being demolished yesterday. The first hour belonged to Australia as the openers continued to milk runs but Warner's dismissal opened the floodgates. Khawaja got a ripper while Smith was given lbw in debatable circumstances. Then, at the stroke of lunch, Marsh was removed as well to leave the hosts in a spot of bother.

OUT! Marsh departs! SA are on a roll here! Full and tailing in from around off, Marsh plays across the line to be pinged on the front pad. Huge lbw appeal which is given by the umpire. Looked quite plumb but Shaun decides to take the review. No bat involved for sure and it's confirmed by both Hot Spot as well as Snicko. Ball Tracker shows it hitting leg stump. Waste of a review to be honest and Australia have lost both their DRS appeals. LUNCH HAS BEEN TAKEN ON DAY 2.
Marsh has been given out lbw. He opts for the review.
Length ball well outside off, too wide to make Marsh play.
Good length on leg stump, Voges works it behind square for a single.
Outside off, Voges makes a comfortable leave.
Full and just outside off, Voges defends it off the back foot.
Flighted outside off, Marsh steps out to that one and blocks it.
Floated on middle, Marsh steps out and clips it towards backward square leg.
Tossed up outside off, Marsh gets well forward to that one and blocks it.
Flighted on middle and leg, Voges uses his feet and clips it through mid-wicket. Nice timing and it'll fetch him three.
Floated on middle, Voges works it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Floated on off, Marsh steps out to that one and whips it down to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, Voges is happy to let it pass.
Good length outside off, no shot offered to that one.
Switches to over the wicket.
Full and on the pads, Marsh clips it down to fine leg for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Marsh hangs back and jabs it towards cover.
Another ball kept well outside off, Marsh shoulders arms to let it pass.
Full and outside off, Marsh doesn't offer a stroke to that one.
Vernon Philander is back on for another spell.
Drifting in from outside off, Voges gets forward and blocks.
Floated outside off, Adam steps out to that one and defends.
Fullish outside off, Voges gets well forward and defends it solidly.
Floated outside off, Voges reaches out to block it out.
Flatter outside off, Voges defends it firmly from the crease.
FOUR! Voges gets off the mark! Fuller on leg stump, Voges gets across to flick but gets it off the inside edge down to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Full and outside off, this one zips away as Marsh lets it pass.
Full and curving into leg stump, Marsh fails to dig it out and is struck on the pads. No time to even appeal for the lbw as the umpire's no ball comes out for overstepping.
Good length angling in from outside off, Marsh makes a leave to that one.
Back of a length outside off, no shot offered to that one.
Pitched up outside off, Marsh gets on the front foot and defends it well.
Good length outside off, no shot offered to that one.
Full and outside off, Marsh defends it well from the crease.
Fullish outside off, Adam reaches out and defends it.
Full and outside off, Voges reaches out and blocks it out.
Flatter on middle and leg, blocked well from the crease by Voges.
Adam Voges is the new man in.

OUT! Maiden Test wicket for Maharaj! What a wicket to start off his career with. Floated and outside off, Smith steps out to work across the line but finds himself in a tangle to be rapped on the pads. Loud appeal for lbw and it's given immediately. Smith isn't happy and decides to review it. No bat involved and that's confirmed by Hot Spot as well as RTS. Ball Tracker shows it's clipping leg stump, so the on-field call will stay. A duck for the Australian skipper. The Proteas are starting to turn things around here. This has been an excellent 45 minutes or so for them.
Smith has been given out lbw. He opts for the review.
Flatter on leg stump, Smith goes back to flick but is struck on the pads. The ball rolls to short leg.
Floated on off, Marsh uses his feet and works it past a diving Faf at mid-wicket. Single taken.
Full and outside off, Smith drives it sweetly towards cover.
Back of a length outside off, Smith hangs back and taps it to the covers.
Steven Smith is the new man in.

OUT! The off pole has gone for a walk! Great ball from Rabada and he is elated. Full and just around off, nips in as Khawaja looks to push tamely at it. Leaves a slight gap between bat and pad but that was enough as the movement sends the off stump for a mini dance. The South Africans wanted this badly especially after Steyn's absence from the field.
Khawaja has been bowled off a ripper. They are checking if Rabada has overstepped.
Length ball outside off, no shot offered to that one by Usman.
Good length outside off, Khawaja reaches out and taps it towards point.
Good length fired well down the leg side, Khawaja misses the flick.
Fuller outside off, blocked well off the front foot.
Another good stop by du Plessis! Tossed up ball around off, Marsh steps out and works it to mid-wicket where Faf makes a good stop, this time to his right.
Floated around off, Marsh reaches out and whips it to mid-wicket where Faf makes a good stop to his left.
Loopy around off, Marsh steps out and tucks it towards short leg.
Drifting in from around off, Marsh gets the stride in and blocks.
Tossed up outside off, defended nicely off the front foot on to the track.
Full and well outside off, Khawaja doesn't offer a shot to that one.
Back of a length outside off, Khawaja hangs back to block but the ball goes off the outer half of the blade towards gully.
Slips this well down the leg side, Khawaja isn't interested to play at that.
Full and angling in from around off, Marsh shuffles and wrists it to mid-wicket for a single.
Fullish outside off, Marsh drives it firmly back to Rabada who stops it well on his followthrough.
Full and outside off, Marsh gets on the front foot and blocks it well.
Loopy outside off, Khawaja camps back and taps it to short mid-wicket.
Floated well outside off, Khawaja reaches out and pushes it towards point.

Steyn is clutching his right shoulder in discomfort. He seems to be in a bad shape and is leaving the field. Not good news for SA especially with the veteran pacer just having picked up a wicket. Maharaj will complete the over.
Length ball outside off, Khawaja looks to cut but ends up chopping it to point.
Good length on off, pushed off the back foot towards mid on.
Good length outside off, Khawaja shoulders arms to that one.
Length ball well outside off, Khawaja doesn't offer a shot to that one.
Very good running! Full ball on leg stump, Marsh shuffles across and clips it sweetly through mid-wicket. The ball will not cross the ropes but the batsmen have done really well to run four.
Fullish on the pads, Marsh flicks it well but straight towards square leg.
Lands this well wide outside off, once again Marsh lets it pass.
Good length well outside off, that's an easy leave for Marsh.
Play and a miss! Length ball angled away from outside off, Marsh gets forward to push at it but is beaten by the movement and bounce. Good ball!
Fullish but too straight by Rabada and Khawaja tucks it through mid-wicket. Won't make the fence but they'll get three.
Good length angling in from outside off, left alone to the keeper.
Switches to around the wicket.
Another full ball outside off, Khawaja bunts it sweetly to mid off where Cook misfields to allow the single.
Full and outside off, Khawaja drives it firmly to mid off.
Good length around off, Khawaja gets well right behind the line and blocks.
Usman Khawaja walks out to bat.

OUT! NO TON FOR WARNER! He only has himself to blame. Length ball angling away outside off, a bit of away movement with extra bounce. Warner flashes at it but gets the thick edge that goes straight to Amla at first slip. Much-needed wicket for the Proteas as Warner walks back disappointed. He knew a big ton was there for the taking. Steyn is absolutely pumped up. Can the Proteas use this opening to make a comeback in the game?
Short of a length outside off, crashed off the back foot to deep point for a single. Maharaj has been put under pressure by the Aussies and he fumbles once more to concede the second run.
Drinks break.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Lands it in the channel outside off, on a length, Marsh pokes inside the line and misses.

Thinking was right from the bowler but not the execution. He attempts to hurl in a scorching yorker but ends ups serving a full toss on middle, Marsh flicks it wide of the fielder at mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Full and around middle and off, Marsh pushes it straight to mid on.
Bouncer around leg, Marsh takes his eyes off the ball and ducks at the last moment.

Good length ball on middle and leg, angling down, Warner tries to turn it on the leg side but misses. It goes off his thigh pad to backward square leg and they cross for a leg bye. David there wasn't interested in the run.
5th Test fifty for Shaun Marsh!

FOUR! Steyn delivers a juicy half-volley outside off, Marsh leans forward and creams his drive through covers for a boundary. A lovely way to reach his fifty. He started scratchily last evening but today has looked a lot composed and is playing a handy knock in this partnership. The Marsh family is all smiles.
Steyn once again bowls it full and around the off stump line, Marsh blocks it solidly.
Bowls it full and on off, Marsh defends it softly off the front foot to covers.
Steyn fires across a full ball outside off, Marsh gets across to stumps and then leaves it alone with a strange followthrough of the bat.
Lands it on a length around off, Warner bunts it down to mid off and picks up a sharp single as the fielder misses his shy at the non-striker's end. A wayward throw.

Full in length on middle and off, nipping away, Warner pushes it with an angled bat through backward point and scampers back for the second run. Maharaj in the deep was on the slower side and Warner was even ready to take the third run.
Change of ends for Dale Steyn.
Keeps his length full again and around off, Marsh defends it off his front foot. End of another unconvincing over by Rabada.
Angles across a full ball outside off, Marsh allows it through with ease.
Back of a length ball on middle, Warner goes back and drags his attempted pull shot off the inside half of the bat. It squirts through mid-wicket for a run. Moves to 92!
Fuller and straighter, Marsh clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Gets his line correct this time but it's too wide outside off to bother the batsman.
Wrong line, Rabada is struggling with his line. In the last over he was bowling the middle and leg line and bowled this one down the leg side. Marsh allows it through.
Movement away from the batsman, Warner allows it through to the keeper.
Bowls it around off, Warner defends it back with a dead bat.

Shout for a catch! A half-hearted one though and the umpire shakes his head. Philander slips a full ball down the leg side, Warner tries flicking but misses. It seems to have clipped his pads and hence there is a deflection. A good diving take by de Kock, but he knew it was off the pads and hence just did a gentle inquiry.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

EDGY FOUR! Philander bowls it on a length and wide outside off, Warner chases it away from his body, has a tame push inside the line and the outside edge speeds through the gap between gully and slips for a boundary.
A bit uppish this time as Marsh flicks a full ball again, this time it's stopped by the square leg fielder with a dive on one bounce.
FOUR! Sharp delivery but once again it's full and on middle, too straight on this occasion, Marsh connects with his flick shot and sends it across through square leg for a boundary.

Bowls it full and down the leg side, Marsh fails to flick and it goes off his pads towards fine leg. Philander who just finished his over seemed to be catching his breath and was late in attacking the ball and hence the batsmen return for the second leg bye.
Fuller in length on middle, Warner flicks it towards square leg and scampers across to the other end. Maharaj picks up the ball but misses his shy at the bowler's end.

FOUR! Not from the middle of the bat but a boundary nonetheless. Rabada offers width outside off, Warner flashes his blade through the line and it comes off the bottom half. He ends up chopping it just wide of the flying gully fielder.
Good length ball on middle and off, Warner defends it off his back foot.
Kagiso Rabada comes on to bowl.
FOUR! Fine shot! Philander serves it full around middle and off, Marsh leans forward and across to flick it sweetly past the left side of Rabada at mid on for a boundary.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Length ball on middle, straightening a touch to cramp the batsman a bit, Marsh tries to keep it out at the last moment and does so with his gloves. It hits him high on the thigh pad as well.
Play and miss! On a length around off, shaping away, Marsh feels for it and gets beaten.
Full in length and outside off, Marsh takes his front leg forward to cover the line and then shoulders arms.
Length delivery outside off, Warner plays from the crease and taps it down to point for a single.
Good leave on this occasion. Outside off, Marsh covers the line and shoulders arms.

Steyn hurls it very full and outside off, once again Marsh is beaten on the drive. Nearly edged it behind. There was a sound though which got the fielders excited but it was of the bat hitting the turf.

Play and a miss! Full and fired outside off, Marsh runs out of patience as he attempts for a booming drive through the line. Ends up missing it completely. And he lost his composure as soon as I mentioned he was looking relaxed.
Lands it full and around off, Marsh defends it solidly from the crease. He has looked a lot more relaxed this morning.
Pitches it full on off, Marsh keeps his body weight inside the crease and defends it with an open faced bat to cover-point.
Full and around off, Marsh brings down a straight bat and defends it back.
Warner has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Appeal for an lbw! Warner tries to flick it from the crease but misses and is hit on the pads. They appeal but it seems to have pitched outside leg. Not given by the umpire.

FOUR! First boundary of the morning! And this will give a sense of calmness to Warner who has looked a bit itchy since morning. Full in length and outside off, David reaches out for it and strokes it powerfully through the gap between mid off and extra cover for a boundary.
Lands it full and on middle, Warner defends it stoutly back to the bowler.
Full and angling away from the southpaw, Marsh defends it off his back foot to the off side. They cross for a single. Much better bowling this morning by South Africa.
Drops it on a fuller length on off, shaping in, Marsh plays it with a loose bottom hand to the leg side.
Play and a miss! Warner is looking a bit itchy! Slanted across a full ball outside off, Warner takes his front leg forward and tries to slap it through the line but misses. No luck for South Africa!
On a full length and around middle, Warner remains back and defends it to the leg side off the inner half of the bat. Should have been forward there.
Strides forward to a full ball and pushes it in the gap at covers for a quick single. Excellent strike rotation.
Nearly drags it on! Full in length and around off, Warner defends it off his back foot and it comes off the inside half of the bat. Rolls wide of the stumps and they pinch a single.
Keeps it full and on middle, Warner gets behind the line and pushes it towards mid on.
Pitches it full and on off, Warner plays a good looking off drive but straight to the fielder.
A touch short in length on off, Marsh goes on the back foot and punches it towards the point fielder.
Full in length and on off, Warner gets back and taps it down towards square leg for a single.
Full in length on middle and off, nipping in a bit, Warner defends it off the inside half of the bat and it pops out off his pads. No short leg there.
Fullish and on off, Warner stays back and opens the face of the bat to push it towards gully. He got a bit squared up there.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Warner defends it from the crease to the leg side.
Tempts Warner with a fuller length ball outside off, there to be driven but David leaves it alone.
Taps a length ball in the gap at covers and scampers across for a single.
Watchfully left this time by Warner. It was once again in the channel outside off.
Play and a miss! Steyn angles across a full length ball outside off, holding its line, Warner flashes at it flat-footed and misses.
Lands it full around leg, Warner defends it off his pads to the leg side.
Fuller in length and on middle, Warner gets behind the line and defends it back to the bowler.
Nice delivery, on a length around off and shaping back in a touch, Warner defends it off his back foot.
Full and angling away from the batsman, Marsh gets forward to cover the line and allows it through.
Marsh has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Lands it around leg and gets it to move back in a bit, Marsh tries to flick but misses and is hit on the thigh pad. A stifled appeal from the bowler but to no avail.
Targets the middle stump and bowls it on a fuller length, Marsh defends it by getting on the front foot.
Angles across a good length ball on off, Warner goes back and punches it through the gap at cover-point for a single.
Philander pitches it full and around off, angling away, Warner has a watchful leave.

FOUR! Nicely played! Back of a length ball around off, not enough room but Marsh creates it for himself by camping back. He then slashes his bat through the line and places his shot right through the gap between slips and gully for a boundary.
Good length delivery in the zone outside off, a hint of away shape, Marsh judges the line nicely and lets it through.
Full and on off, defended off the front foot by Marsh.
Marsh chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Angles across a length ball outside off, Marsh covers the line and leaves it again.
Bowls it in the channel outside off, 134.6 kph, Marsh allows it through to the keeper.
Dale Steyn to steam in from the other end. Three slips and a gully.

Too straight in line on this occasion, Marsh eases it through mid-wicket and Maharaj chases it. He puts in a slide but fails to pull it back. By the time the mid on fielder cuts it off, they take the third run.
Beaten! Philander hurls across a full ball on off, nipping away a bit, Marsh tries defending it off his front foot but gets beaten.
Keeps it full and close to the off stump line, Marsh gets forward, brings his bat and pad together and defends it safely.
Good length ball angling across the batsman, Marsh covers the line and shoulders arms.
Full in length on middle and leg, angling down, Marsh tucks it through square leg and returns for the second run.
Starts with a gentle length delivery in the channel outside off, Marsh has a good look at it before leaving it alone.

It's time to get going. The South African players are in a huddle. A big day ahead for them as they have their backs to the wall in this Test match. Out come David Warner and Shaun Marsh, the overnight Aussie batsmen. Vernon Philander to start proceedings. Two slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

Hello and welcome to day two of the first Test between Australia and South Africa at the WACA, Perth. A strong bowling performance followed by an aggressive period with the bat saw the hosts end the opening day on a dominating note. The deficit is 137 and with all 10 wickets intact, Australia will hope to bat the visitors out of the game. South Africa will need early wickets today or else it could slip away soon. The action isn't far away.
......DAY 2, SESSION 1......

Statistician Ric Finlay sums it up in this tweet. "Fantastic day at the WACA. Nothing beats Test cricket in its current form. Doesn't need to be any different. Tinker with the other formats." Do join us at 0800 IST tomorrow for another cracker of a day. Cheers!

Renowned broadcaster, Glenn Mitchell tweets, "An opening day at the WACA Ground that may define the series ... RSA all out 242 ... AUS 0/105 with Warner 73 (61) and S Marsh 29." Indeed. It has been a dominating day for the hosts. This is also the first century stand for the opening wicket for Australia at home against South Africa, since 2002! At the SCG, Matthew Hayden and Justin Langer hammered 219 for the first wicket.

The deficit is already down to 137 and with all the wickets intact, Australia have wrested the advantage in their favour. South Africa have their backs to the wall and will end up playing catch up cricket if they fail to strike early tomorrow morning. We are expecting a cracking day 2 as well.

The Proteas would have hoped that their bowlers will return the favour to the Aussies but they weren't penetrative enough. And to add to their misery, Australia's gun player David Warner was firing bullets from the word go. Along with a not-so-convincing partner in Shaun Marsh, he has provided a solid platform to Australia. Warner, however, got a reprieve on 17 when he was lbw but Philander had overstepped. Since then, the Aussie opener has not looked back and made the Africans pay dearly for it.

The Australian summer is off and running in grand style for the home team. Apart from losing the toss in the morning, nothing much went against them. Their bowlers did an amazing job to restrict South Africa under 250 in spite of an attacking knock by Quinton de Kock. Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood were the destroyers-in-chief as they hunted down seven wickets between them.

Tossed up delivery around off, David Warner prods forward and blocks it out watchfully. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1! Warner comes up to Marsh, gives him a fist punch as Australia head to the dressing room without any hiccup.

FOUR! More runs! Third one of the over, this! Drags his length back but it's again outside off. Warner who is all set won't let that go waste. Gets back and cuts it behind point for a boundary. No need to run for those.
FOUR! Sweetly done to bring up the 100 for Australia! Floated ball outside off, Warner lunges forward and drives it exquisitely through the cover region for another gorgeous boundary.
Gives this one a bit more flight around off, Warner defends it watchfully.
Gets back and defends it down gently.
FOUR! Last over of the day and Warner is not afraid to go after it. Tossed up ball outside off, Warner makes a long stride forward and drills it through covers for a boundary. Delightful stroke!
In the corridor outside off, SM lets it go.

Whiskerrrrr! Back of a length delivery on off, straightens a touch after pitching. Marsh comes forward to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge to the keeper. The bowler appeals for a caught behind but the umpire turns it down. Replays show there was no wood involved.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Good length ball on off, Shaun looks to defend but the ball zips through the surface but somehow keeps it out.
Strays it on the pads, Marsh flicks it through square leg. Some good running between the wickets allows them to come back for the second.
Angles it on the pads, Warner gets back and nudges it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up around off, Shaun covers the line and punches it back to the bowler.
Slower through the air and around off, Marsh hangs back and defends it back to Maharaj.
Short and outside off, Warner gets back and punches it through covers for a single.
Tossed up ball around middle, Warner gets across and defends it towards the leg side.
A nice loopy ball around middle and leg, Marsh gets back and works it through square leg for a single.
Tossed up ball around middle, Marsh comes forward to defend but it goes off the inner part of the bat past short leg for a couple.
Time for spin as KESHAV MAHARAJ will roll his arm!
Fullish in length and angling in, SM nudges it towards the leg side for one.
Fuller in length on middle, worked towards the man at mid on.
In the channel outside off, Shaun lifts his bat and allows it to go through.
Serves it on the pads, Warner works it through square leg for an easy single.
Good length ball on middle and off, Warner taps it down.
On a length and angling in, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Hurls it on the pads, too easy for Marsh as he simply tucks it behind square on the on side for a single to keep strike.
Fuller in length on middle, Warner flicks it towards wide mid on for a single.
Fuller in length and just around the off stump line, Davey presses forward and keeps it out on the off side.
Good length ball on middle and off, DW defends it back to Philander.
Warner gets back and shows a straight bat.
Pitches it on off, Warner blocks it out.

FOUR! Pulled away in style! Kagiso digs in a short ball on middle and leg, Marsh swivels and pulls it towards fine leg. The fielder comes sprinting to his left, puts in a dive but fails to stop it from crossing the ropes.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, flicked towards wide mid on.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
A harmless ball outside off, Shaun says I have nothing to do with that one.
Shaun Marsh stays behind the line and pushes it towards  backward point.
Rabada bowls a length ball on off, David stays back and pushes it towards covers for a single.
Outside off, Marsh is happy to let de Kock collect it.
In the channel outside off, Shaun prods forward to defend but gets beaten again.
Fuller and angling on the pads, flicked towards the man at short mid-wicket.
Strays it on the pads, tucked towards fine leg for a single.
A length ball outside off, Warner looks to punch this one but gets it off the bottom edge towards the bowler.
On a good length and around off, Warner stays in the crease and taps it down on the off side.
Marsh draws forward to defend but is beaten all ends.
Touch short on the leg stump, it's whipped through square leg by David for one.
Short of a length delivery on off, Marsh looks to pull but doesn't quite get it off the middle of the bat. The ball goes towards mid on and the batsmen take a single.
Covers the line on this length delivery and defends it back to Rabada.
Good length outside off, SM makes a watchful leave to the keeper.
Full and sprayed down the leg side, Marsh looks to flick but fails to get any wood on it.
Good length ball on middle and off, Warner defends it on the off side.
On the pads, Shaun clips it behind square for a single.
In the corridor outside off, SM has got nothing to offer on that one.
Comes forward a bit and defends it down gently.
Angles it on middle, Shaun misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
On a length and around off, Marsh looks to defend but the extra bounce takes him by surprise as the ball goes off the gloves, then onto his shoulder and dips just in front of the man at second slip.
Change of ends for PHILANDER!

FIVE OVERTHROWS! Good length delivery on off, Marsh taps it towards covers and wants a single. Warner agrees and there is a shy at the bowler's end but it misses. The fielder doing the back up dives but to no avail and the ball races away to the mid-wicket fence for a boundary. Bonus runs!
Another easy leave for Marsh.

Goodness me. David Warner really loves the WACA. This is his 5th score of 50 or more at this venue. He has reached 50 off just 39 balls. Balls taken to reach fifty by him in Tests at the WACA - 36, 39, 56, 56, 57.
Good length ball around off, Marsh lifts his bat and lets it through to the keeper.
No ball!  Defended off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single. No Ball has been signalled by the umpire.
22nd Test fifty for David Warner, 3rd against SA!

FOUR! Ahh.. this bloke just loves batting here, ain't he? Was shaky a bit at the start but have a look at him now. Good length delivery on off, Warner drives it on the up through covers. No one even bothered moving and Warner gets a sizzling fifty here. Once again a good start at the top has been provided by the southpaw.
Too wide outside off to trouble David.
Good length ball on off, pushed towards point off the back foot.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Runs coming thick and fast at the moment! Good length delivery outside off, Warner steers it past point and gets another boundary to his name. Cruising towards another Test fifty here.

SIX! Shot Davey! Back of a length delivery outside off, Warner uses the pace and bounce as he arches back, keeps the bat skywards and plays the upper cut to send the ball sailing over the third man fence for a biggie all the way. Oh dear, Warner is down on the ground after playing that shot as he loses his balance.
50 up for Australia! Touch fuller and around off, pushed towards covers for a single.
Gets back and clips it towards square leg for a single.
On a good length and outside off, Warner punches it towards covers. The fielder puts in a dive but the ball goes through which allows them to come back for a couple.
Defended from within the crease.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Good length ball on off, Marsh lets it go.
Fullish on off, pushed through covers for a single.
FOUR! Fuller in length and served wide outside off, Warner throws his bat at it as the ball goes off the top edge and over the slip cordon for a boundary towards third man.

A loud shout for a caught behind! Rabada starts off with a back of a length ball on off, Warner looks to slash this one through the off side but fails to do so. de Kock collects the ball and they all go up in an appeal. The umpire stays unmoved. Rabada does not want to take the review and signals so to his team mates. Nonetheless, a good start to the spell.
First change then, KAGISO RABADA is brought into the attack, replacing Philander.
Good length on off, Marsh looks to defend but fails to put bat on ball.

FOUR! Down the ground! Fuller in length and on off, Marsh leans into it and drives it past the non-striker for a boundary. There is no mid off and the fielder from extra cover was always going to come second best to the ball.
Outside off, SM leaves it alone.
FOUR! Gets it this time! Short and going down leg, Shaun swivels a bit and pulls it towards fine leg for a racy boundary. Good shot!

Sharp reflexes from Bavuma! Good length delivery on middle, Marsh tries to play the controlled pull shot but it goes on the bounce to Bavuma at short leg who quickly releases the ball with a back flick. It goes over the stumps but good work. You need someone like him to do the job.
A brisk single! Back of a length delivery outside off, Warner stands tall and punches it towards covers for a quick single. Warner and Steyn are seen sharing a smile near the bowler's landing area.
On a length and tailing back in, Marsh was in two minds whether to leave it or play at it and in the end he misses to put bat on ball and is hit on the pads.
Straight to the fielder! Fuller and angling it on middle, SM gets across a touch and flicks it. Much to his dismay the ball goes straight to the man at short mid-wicket.
Touch short and served around off, Marsh gets behind the line and answers it with the full face of the bat.
Stands tall and defends this one with bat and pad together.
In the channel outside off, Shaun Marsh drops his wrists down and lets it go.
Swoosh! Philander hurls it on a length on off, Marsh gets behind the line to defend but fails to do so as the ball almost kisses the outside edge before it goes into de Kock's gloves.
Banged in hard on middle, Warner sits under it. An eventful over from Dale!
Fuller and around off, defended off the front foot solidly.

FOUR! Edged and just over! Warner is having some luck by his side here. Survived an LBW appeal and now two edges but finds the fence. Short of a length delivery just outside off, Warner flashes hard at it as the ball goes off the outside edge and flies over a leaping Amla at first slip for a boundary towards third man.

FOUR! Top edge! Short of a length delivery on middle, Warner winds up for the pull but is a bit cramped for room. He still continues with the shot and luckily for him the edge files over the keeper's head and races down to the fence for a boundary. Steyn shares a wry smile.
Shaun Marsh is off the mark! It has taken him 17 balls to do so. Back of a length delivery on middle, Marsh rolls his wrists and pulls it through square leg for a single. That should ease his nerves.
Good length delivery on middle, Marsh hangs back and answers it with a straight bat.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Sliding down the leg side, Warner tries flicking but misses. Good job done by de Kock to stop the ball to his right.
FOUR! Lovely shot to ease some pressure. Warner strides forward to a full ball and strokes it elegantly through mid off for a boundary.
Sharp delivery again, around off and extra bounce, Warner gets an inside edge on the pads as he looks to defend from the crease.

IT'S A NO BALL! No need to look further. But we will still let you know what happened on this ball. It's a good length ball on leg, Warner fails to defend it from the crease and gets rapped on the pads. They appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Du Plessis goes for the review and as already mentioned Philander was found to be overstepping. Hawk Eye shows that it hit Warner in line and was hitting the leg stump. A costly no ball for the Proteas.
Huge shout for an lbw. The umpire remains unmoved. Faf du Plessis has taken the DRS.
An uncomfortable delivery, not rising much, Warner tries to work it across with a jump but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.

Brave leave! Philander dishes out a length ball on off, nipping in a bit, Warner trusts the bounce and shoulders arms. It goes over the off stump. De Kock cannot believe it and the bowler has his hands on his head.
Good length ball on off, extra bounce, Marsh jumps on the back foot and defends it off the inside half of the bat. End of a testing over and Marsh remains on zero!
Steyn serves it on a length and wide outside off, Marsh allows it through.
Steyn digs in a short ball around leg, Marsh is early into the shot and takes a blow on his body. Clearly not comfortable with short pitch stuff and South Africa have done their homework.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him. South Africa are working on a plan.

Nearly the ploy to keep bat-pad works! Excellent short pitch bowling, Marsh stands tall, takes his eyes off the ball and tries to fend. It comes off his gloves and goes on one bounce to Bavuma at short leg. He is very sharp with his reflexes, arguably the best going around at the moment.
A short leg comes into place now.
Extra bounce from a shortish length around middle, Marsh jumps and turns it on the leg side, finds square leg. Remains on nought!

FOUR! A mere push and it's a boundary! Warner is motoring, he loves playing at this venue. A half-volley around middle and off, Warner gets forward with a straight bat and caresses it down the ground for a boundary.
Bowls it on the driving length outside off, a tempter, Warner watches it carefully and lets it through to the keeper.
A little short and around off, Warner goes on his toes and taps it down to point.
Lands it full and on off, Warner gets forward and pushes it straight to mid off.
FOUR! This one is all timing! Philander angles across a full ball around off, Warner stays back and pushes it with an angled bat. Times it superbly and it races through point for a boundary.
FOUR! Boom! Width on offer outside off, it's on the shorter side as well, Warner latches onto it and swats it through covers for a powerful boundary.
Touch short and around off, Marsh looks to cut but gets it off the bottom part of the bat towards point.
Banged short on middle, at 143.6 kph, Shaun Marsh ducks to evade it.

Chance of a run out! Angles it on middle, Marsh gets back and taps it towards mid-wicket. He sets off for a single but then Warner sends him back. Keshav Maharaj charges to the ball and hurls an underarm throw at the striker's end. Marsh gets back in but could have been in trouble as he slipped while returning back. In the end no damage done.
Length delivery on middle, Marsh covers the line and defends it towards the leg side.
Hits the deck hard on middle, at 143 clicks. Shaun Marsh does well to evade it at the right time otherwise would have been hit on the helmet.
On a length and around off, Marsh stays back and defends it down.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, David lifts his bat and lets it go through to the keeper.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Good length delivery on off, Warner gets on the top of the bounce and crunches it through covers. Once it pierced the gap it had boundary written all over it.

No ball! Lovely bowling! But... he will have to reload as he overstepped! Touch full on off, holding its line as well. Warner gets on the front foot to defend but the ball whizzes past the outside edge to the keeper.
Fuller in length outside off, Warner drives it towards mid off.
Fuller in length and angling on the pads, Warner gets forward and defends it down the track as the ball rolls back to Philander.
On a length and curling back in this time with some bounce on it. Warner looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. No LBW appeal as height was an issue there.
Back of a length delivery on off, rising off the deck. Warner stays in the crease and fends it towards covers.
VERNON PHILANDER to share the new cherry from the other end!
In the channel outside off, Shaun shoulders his arms to that one.
Beaten! On a good length and outside off, Marsh looks to poke at it but gets beaten. Nice carry to the keeper.
Fuller in length on off, Marsh defends it towards point.
Warner is off the mark! Good length delivery, just outside off, Warner taps it towards covers and scurries across for a quick single.
Back of a length ball outside off, Warner gets back and defends it on the off side.
Starts with a shortish delivery down the leg side, Warner hops and tries to turn it down the leg side but misses.
